The “Wednesday” actor appeared Tuesday on Andy Cohen’s “Watch What Happens Live,” where the late-night host asked Ricci about her relationship with Cher.

“Unfortunately, she’s still mad at me,” Ricci told Cohen during her appearance, adding that the iconic singer “holds a grudge” and revealing what went down.

The two starred in the 1990 film “Mermaids,” where Cher played the mother of Ricci and Winona Ryder. It seems the two got on well — until an interview seemingly soured their relationship.

“Well, when I was 19, I did some Rolling Stone thing, and they interviewed her,” Ricci shared. “Maybe it wasn’t Rolling Stone. It might have been Première, but they interviewed her, and she said all these things that were not that amazing about me.”

The actor said Cher immediately tried to remedy the situation.

“She left me a voicemail about how journalists are always trying to get the worst things, and blah blah blah,” Ricci said. “And she was so sorry.”

But because Ricci was 19, she said, she “didn’t return that message.”

“I’ve reached out to her since and gotten radio silence,” the actor said. “I adore her. She’s the best. And I absolutely 100% can imagine being Cher and being like, ‘Oh my god, they 100% misquoted me. I’m going to call this young person and explain to her that they misquoted me.’”

“And then the gall of that young person to not return the call and be like, ‘Oh my god, Cher, it’s OK. I love you so much,’” Ricci said. “I would be so pissed. I get it.”

HuffPost reached out to reps for Cher for further comment.
